subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different aspects of their purchase are Amazon reviewers actually talking about?

judge.implied_focus: The aspect/dimension of the purchase experience that each Amazon review actually discusses (review topical facets, differentiated by product type)

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Establishes the type of purchase, which conditions which aspects are relevant (content quality for media vs. functional performance for physical goods). Serves as a contextual anchor for the aspect decomposition.

per_column.name: functional_performance_verdict
per_column.rationale: Captures the functional/performance aspect reviewers talk about for physical products -- a distinct, data-inferable facet of the purchase.

per_column.name: content_quality_dimension
per_column.rationale: Captures the content/artistic aspect (plot, acting, writing) relevant to media purchases -- a complementary facet, not a restatement of the functional one.

per_column.name: comparison_reference_type
per_column.rationale: Captures whether/how reviewers frame the purchase relative to alternatives -- a genuine and distinct aspect of what reviewers discuss.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively centre on a single coherent focus: the differentiated aspects of the purchase that reviewers actually talk about. Three columns are true topical facets (functional performance, content quality, comparison framing) and use meaningful 'not_present/no_comparison' sentinels to mark which aspect is engaged per review, which is exactly what the query ('what different aspects... actually talking about') asks. product_category is a sensible conditioning anchor rather than an aspect itself, but it strengthens rather than scatters the focus by explaining why different aspect columns apply to different rows. The structure is at a useful granularity with differentiated sub-values (narrative_plot, pacing, does_not_work, etc.), not a single restatement or generic noise. The focus is clearly actionable: an analyst can quantify which aspects dominate, segment by product type, and target improvements. Minor deductions: some overlap in coverage across media-oriented columns and the aspect set is not exhaustive (e.g., price/value, shipping/service aspects are absent), slightly narrowing the 'different aspects' claim.
